Subject: Commitment timeline & sequencing for MSA / DPA / Order

Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for the product demo yesterday. We want to lock a realistic timeline for legal and procurement so our security and contracts teams can calendar review windows. High level asks from our side:

- Confirm which documents must be fully executed before we can get to a PO (MSA + Order Form required; DPA preferred to be signed or on a parallel track).
- Expected lead time for SOC2 artefacts and any security evidence we asked for.
- Whether Redwood can accept PO + post-sign billing for the pilot (trial) or if signature is required first.

We are targeting a pilot kickoff in the first week of November. Can you outline a recommended sequencing (who signs first, expected IP/insurance clauses that typically slow you down, and a realistic close date assuming a standard one-week internal review at MedFlow legal)?

Hi Sarah —

Thanks — great next steps. Below is a recommended sequencing that has worked for similar mid-market customers and should keep your target kickoff intact if we stay on schedule: 

1) We circulate a redlined MSA + DPA in parallel (we typically accept focused redlines on liability, data processing clauses, and security controls).
2) At the same time Redwood will send a draft Order Form (price/term/SKU) for your procurement to review. The Order Form can be attached to the MSA or executed as a standalone document depending on your preference.
3) Legal review window at MedFlow: 5–7 business days (you noted one week) — during this time procurement can provision a PO draft.
4) Execution: if MSA + Order Form are signed, we can start provisioning dedicated pilot capacity; if DPA is pending, we can proceed under a DPA-in-progress exception where technical work begins after a PO and mutual NDAs are in place.
5) SOC2 summary: I attached our SOC2 summary and the typical evidence bundle we provide; that usually satisfies initial security gating for pilot access.

Quick call ask: can we book a 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk the sequence and confirm internal owners on your side? I’ll include Karthik (contracts) and Laura (finance/billing) on the call.

Attachments: draft_order_form_v0.3.pdf, redwood_soc2_summary.pdf

Thanks,

Thanks Rishi + Sarah — adding a couple of pragmatic notes from the contracts side: 

- Typical gating items that add most time: (1) indemnity/limitation language, (2) data residency/processing controls in DPA, (3) insurance certificates. If MedFlow needs custom caps, expect legal back-and-forth.
- Suggestion: MedFlow legal flags anything nonstandard in a single consolidated redline document. That reduces cycle time.
- If you want the fastest close: accept standard Redwood MSA (we can limit changes to a short list) + sign Order Form; run DPA concurrently. This lets procurement raise a PO against the signed Order Form and get technical access while DPA completes.

I’ll create a short acceptance checklist for Laura to confirm billing terms and for Monica to confirm trial provisioning requirements.

Attachments: proposed_msa_redlines.docx (placeholder with common clauses)

-karthik

Sarah —

Appreciate the clarity. Confirming what we agreed: 

- Plan: Redwood will send a clean MSA (with limited tracked changes where necessary), a DPA template (for parallel review), and the draft Order Form via DocuSign EOD 2026-09-14.
- Pilot provisioning: Redwood can provision pilot access on receipt of an approved PO referencing the Order Form and a signed Order Form or signature via DocuSign. If legal needs more time on the DPA, we will accept a DPA-in-progress exception with an agreed completion window of 10 business days.
- Insurance: attaching a certificate template and our insurer contact details in the DocuSign packet.
- Owners: MedFlow legal (Sarah) — legal review; procurement — PO; Redwood contracts (Karthik) — negotiate redlines; Redwood billing (Laura) — invoice terms; Redwood ops (Monica) — provisioning.

Next steps (timeline):
- 2026-09-14 EOD: Redwood sends MSA + DPA + Order Form via DocuSign.
- 2026-09-15 to 2026-09-21: MedFlow legal review (target 5 business days).
- If signed by 2026-09-21 and PO issued same day, pilot provisioning targeted for first week of November (contingent on capacity).

I’ll send the DocuSign link and the attachments now. Thanks — looking forward to progressing this.
